name: JIATF-401 Industry Engagement (official mailbox)

why: Official on-ramp for capability submissions, industry days, characterization events.

name: Brig. Gen. Matt Ross
title: Director, JIATF-401; senior C-UAS advisor to CJCS; dual-hatted under DRPM-UxS
channel: Via JIATF-401 industry mailbox / industry days; Army public affairs for media
why: Sets requirements and runs test-then-buy. Publicly asked for non-explosive kinetic interceptors for homeland use and low-cost attritable, software-defined solutions.

name: Col. Tony Lindh
title: Director of Acquisition / Rapid Acquisitions Lead, JIATF-401
channel: Via JIATF-401 industry mailbox
why: Runs the $7B Marketplace IDIQ program; said more IDIQs would be signed by end of October 2026.

name: Maj. Mike Hapner
title: C-UAS Marketplace Lead
channel: cuas.mil vendor application (vetting: business verification, export review, product evaluation)
why: Owns the marketplace listing and vetting that let buyers across DoD and the interagency order directly.

name: Brent G. Ingraham
title: Assistant Secretary of the Army (Acquisition, Logistics & Technology)
channel: Industry days (spoke at the LCI Industry Day, June 23, 2026)
why: Army acquisition executive over the JIATF-401 IDIQs and drones.mil; insists on open architecture.

name: Dan Driscoll
title: Secretary of the Army
channel: Public statements only; engage through program offices
why: Champion of cheap interceptors ('right end of the cost curve'); bought 13,000 Merops in 8 days.

name: Lt. Gen. Francisco Lozano
title: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires & Director, RCCTO (nominated)
channel: PAE Fires / RCCTO industry engagement; Army Contracting Command–Redstone (W31P4Q)
why: PAE Fires owns C-UAS programs of record (Coyote/LIDS, E-HEL, IFPC-HPM, Grizzly selection with JIATF-401).

name: Brig. Gen. Guy Yelverton
title: Capability Portfolio Executive, Defensive Fires
channel: xTech / LCI program: usarmy.xtech@army.mil
why: Leads the Low-Cost Interceptor program; the xTech|Apex Intercept partner.

name: Army xTech Program (FUZE)
title: Prize competitions and on-ramps
channel: usarmy.xtech@army.mil; https://pit.army.mil/pathway/xtech/
why: Non-dilutive prize money and a route to Army program offices; ran xTechCounterStrike and xTech|Apex Intercept.

name: Gen. Gregory Guillot
title: Commander, U.S. Northern Command & NORAD
channel: NORTHCOM public affairs; Flyaway Kit program
why: Homeland C-UAS synchronizer; reports 1-2 base incursions per day; NORTHCOM has listed net/streamer drones among approved homeland methods.

name: Brig. Gen. Curtis King
title: Commanding General, 10th Army Air & Missile Defense Command
channel: Project Flytrap (with 52nd ADA Brigade) vendor solicitations
why: Operational user of Merops in Europe; Project Flytrap is the Army's European field test of C-UAS vendors.

name: Owen West
title: Director, Defense Innovation Unit
channel: DIU CSO portal: https://www.diu.mil/work-with-us/open-solicitations
why: DIU is the Pentagon's designated front door for unmanned/autonomous commercial companies (June 2026); ran Counter-UAS NEXT and C-UAS sensing CSOs.

name: David Payne
title: Acting Director, Autonomous Warfare portfolio (includes Counter-UAS)
channel: DIU solicitations
why: Portfolio that issues C-UAS CSOs.

name: Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Unmanned Systems (DRPM-UxS)
title: Single joint integrator for UxS and counter-UxS (director not yet named)
org: Office of the Deputy Secretary of War (Steve Feinberg)
channel: Watch for the appointment; JIATF-401 and DAWG directors are dual-hatted under it
why: Will set unified requirements and marketplaces for counter-unmanned systems from FY27.

name: Col. Andrew Konicki (as of 2024 — verify current)
title: Program Manager, Ground Based Air Defense (PM GBAD), PEO Land Systems
channel: MCSC / PEO LS industry briefs (Modern Day Marine)
why: Owns MADIS/L-MADIS; USMC also runs Anduril's I-CsUAS installation program.

name: USASOC C-sUAS Open Call (via SOFWERX/Vulcan)
title: Prototype funding $200K-$2M
channel: Vulcan-SOF submission portal (deadline 2026-12-01)
why: Fast, small-dollar first customer for a portable interceptor.

name: Pedro Allende
title: Under Secretary for Science & Technology
channel: DHS S&T; DHS C-UAS IDIQ (via Track-1 primes)
why: Runs the $1.5B department-wide C-UAS IDIQ; wants OTA authority back to move faster.

name: Justin Napolitano
title: Chief Security Officer, DHS Management Directorate
channel: DHS Office of the Chief Security Officer
why: Department-wide C-UAS requirements for fixed sites, mobile ops and special events.

name: Markwayne Mullin
title: Secretary of Homeland Security
channel: Public statements
why: Acknowledged that DHS defensive drone capability lags; weighing a DHS C-UAS joint task force.

name: FEMA Grant Programs Directorate — C-UAS Grant Program
title: $500M over two years (FY26 $250M awarded; FY27 $250M to all states/territories)
channel: FEMA Grants News (fema-grants-news@fema.dhs.gov, 800-368-6498); State Administrative Agencies (e.g., Cal OES C-UASGrantProgram@caloes.ca.gov)
why: Grantees (state homeland security offices) are the buyers; vendors need to be on the authorized-technology path.

name: FBI National Counter-UAS Training Center (NCUTC)
title: SLTT certification schoolhouse, Huntsville AL (opened Nov 2025)
channel: FBI Critical Incident Response Group
why: Every SLTT mitigation operator, including for in-flight physical interception, must certify here. Training equipment choices shape what police buy.

name: Kash Patel
title: Director, FBI
channel: Public statements
why: FBI co-owns SLTT C-UAS policy with DHS; foiled the drone-and-sniper plot on UFC Freedom 250.

name: Interagency Authorized Technologies List process (DOJ/DHS/FAA/FCC/NTIA)
title: Decides which C-UAS technology categories SLTT may use
channel: Docket FBI-2026-0001 (IFR comments closed ~Sept 4, 2026); DHS S&T and FBI CIRG
why: Physical capture is not expected on the initial (RF-only) list. Getting a physical-interception category added is a prerequisite for state and local sales.

name: Kaizen Labs (Nikhil Reddy, CEO)
title: Builder/operator of cuas.mil under a $15M OTA
channel: Company
why: Runs the marketplace platform's vendor onboarding tooling.

name: UK MOD National Armaments Director Group — LCADE
title: Low-Cost Air Defence Effectors (with LEAP partners Poland, France, Italy, Germany)
channel: UK Defence and Security Accelerator / NAD Group calls
why: Funds SME interceptors; LEAP's next phase picks scalable production across 5 nations — an allied export route.

name: Col. Jason Idleman
title: Chief, Multi-Domain Operations Division
channel: Via JIATF-401 industry mailbox
why: Operational lead quoted on Domestic Shield awards.

name: Michelle Self
title: Deputy, Rapid Acquisition Division
channel: Via JIATF-401 industry mailbox
why: Runs rapid commitments (e.g., $600M in ~1 month for Epic Fury, World Cup, Domestic Shield).

name: Army G-TEAD Marketplace
title: Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate marketplace
channel: G-TEAD marketplace submissions (xTech winners get placement)
why: Merops was fast-tracked through G-TEAD; xTech winners get placement. The demonstrated Army fast lane for interceptor drones.

name: Sen. Roger Wicker
title: Chairman, Senate Armed Services Committee
channel: SASC staff (professional staff members for airland/emerging threats)
why: Publicly championing cost-effective counter-drone production.

name: DHS Program Executive Office for UAS & C-UAS
title: Department-wide drone/counter-drone acquisition office (est. Jan 2026; leader not publicly named in coverage)
channel: DHS Office of Industry Partnership / S&T; brief through DHS C-UAS IDIQ Track-1 primes
why: Single DHS program office for C-UAS buys; ran $115M of World Cup/America250 investments.

name: Army Contracting Command–Detroit Arsenal (office W6QK ACC-DTA; award prefix W912CH)
title: Contracting office behind JIATF-401's FY2025–26 C-UAS buys
channel: Watch SAM.gov for W912CH solicitations; recent C-UAS buys were competed under simplified acquisition with 5–50 offers, and some were small-business set-asides (e.g., W912CH25R0082)
why: Issued the AV Titan order, DroneShield fixed-site/ISV and IRK buys, Echodyne EchoShield, SmartShooter, Anduril Lattice IBCS-M integration and a C-sUAS portfolio study. This is where JIATF-401 money turns into contracts.

name: Army Contracting Command–Redstone (W6QK ACC-RSA; award prefix W31P4Q)
title: Contracting office for PAE Fires C-UAS programs of record
channel: SAM.gov W31P4Q notices
why: Coyote, M-LIDS, FS-LIDS and the SkyWall buy (W31P4Q26C0012).

name: DLA Troop Support — special operational equipment prime vendors (Atlantic Diving Supply, W.S. Darley, Noble, Quantico Tactical, SupplyCore)
title: Catalogue channel for unit-level C-UAS buys
channel: Get listed in a prime vendor's catalogue once the product is mature
why: DLA has bought DroneBuster, EnforceAir2, SMASH 2000L and Dedrone through these primes ($249.5M in the ledger).

name: Maj. Gen. Curtis Taylor
title: Commander, Joint Task Force-Southern Border
channel: Through NORTHCOM / JIATF-401; JTF-SB public affairs for media
why: Runs the highest-volume homeland C-UAS mission (378 cartel drones detected in about five weeks, Aug–Sep 2026); uses lasers, jammers, kinetic and non-kinetic options.

name: Project Manager Close Combat Systems (PEO Ammunition)
title: Army program office named as the Merops transition candidate
org: U.S. Army PEO Ammunition, Picatinny Arsenal
channel: PEO Ammunition industry engagement; watch for interceptor-drone program-of-record notices
why: If interceptor drones become an Army program of record, this office is the likely owner.

name: Maj. Cole Price
title: Assistant Capability Manager, JIATF-401
channel: Through JIATF-401 industry mailbox
why: Capability manager on the Bumblebee V2 collision-interceptor buy.

channel: JIATF401CSO@army.mil (published on the ACC–Detroit Arsenal CSO fact sheet)
why: The official route for CSO questions; solution briefs go through the SAM.gov notice.

name: Maj. Joe Amoroso
title: Deputy Chief of Strategic Initiatives, JIATF-401
channel: Through JIATF-401 industry mailbox
why: Co-author and spokesperson for the JIATF-401 counter-drone handbook (doctrine).

name: Mike (Micheal) Torphy
title: Unit Chief / counter-UAS program lead, FBI Critical Incident Response Group
channel: FBI CIRG; National Counter-UAS Training Center, Huntsville
why: Runs FBI counter-drone training and certification, testified to the Senate Judiciary on SLTT authority (cited in the IFR), and is already planning C-UAS for the 2028 Olympics.

title: Director for Emerging Threats, National Security Council
channel: Through the Federal Task Force to Restore American Airspace Sovereignty (EO 14305)
